Why a torch

Long before anyone had a flashlight, a dried mullein stalk dipped in wax was how you carried light across a dark yard. The plant picked up names for it along the way — hag's taper, candlewick, witch's candle.

It was never only a lamp. Torches were carried in processions, lit at the turn of the seasons, and burned through the night for protection and clear thinking, particularly around Samhain when the year thins out. Part tool, part tradition, and still both.

Meet Marli

I've always felt at home in the mountains, the same with my family before me.

There's a peace that comes from watching things grow, wild and free. A calm that rocks you to sleep under the blanket of the Milky Way, when the only sound for miles and miles is the woods.

The mountain I love as an adult, I share with three generations of my father's family. I've learned what grows, where it grows, and sometimes I even give my plants an extra drink with moon water that I make from the spring at the top of our mountain.

There is healing here.

Everything I sell, I make at my cottage kitchen table or on tables under the trees while a breeze blows through my soul. The batches are small, filled with love and intention, and I look forward to seeing where my products find their home.

How ordering works

No accounts, no checkout maze. Put things in your basket and send it over.

  1. Fill your basket

    Add what you'd like from the shelf. Change your mind as many times as you want.

  2. Send it to Marli

    One tap sends your list by text or email, with your name and any notes.

  3. She confirms it

    Usually within a few hours. She'll check stock and send you a payment link.

  4. It ships or you swing by

    Packed in paper and mailed anywhere in the US, or picked up here on the mountain.
